questions.title: Planning an experiment — wind turbine & power of moving air

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Diagram: a model wind turbine (blades of length L, swept area A) on a bench, a fan positioned in line with the turbine so the air flows over the blades; a resistor R connected in series with an ammeter across the turbine terminals; the speed v of the air and the atmospheric pressure P and temperature T indicated.
Procedure and measurements: vary the air speed v (independent variable — change the fan speed, the fan–turbine distance, or the fan p.d.) and measure the current I in the resistor (dependent variable), keeping A and R (and P, T) constant. Measure T with a thermometer (T = θ/°C + 273). Measure L with a rule and A = πL² (repeat at several positions/blades and average). Measure v with an anemometer/air-speed meter (or P with a manometer/pressure gauge). Determine R with an ohmmeter (or R = V/I).
Analysis: plot a graph of I² against v³. The relationship is valid if a straight line through the origin is produced (for lg I against lg v, a straight line of gradient 1.5). From I²R = QAPv³/(2T): gradient = QAP/(2TR), so Q = gradient × 2TR/(AP).
Controls: keep A, R, P and T constant. Wait for a steady/constant air flow and current before reading. Clamp the turbine/fan to the bench. Check that the temperature/pressure are constant by measuring before and after.
Safety: keep away from the (moving) fan/turbine blades (or use a screen); wear goggles to protect the eyes from the air stream/dust. Repeat readings and average.

questions.title: Analysis of data — orbits of Saturn’s moons (Kepler’s law)

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
T = 2πrⁿ/k, so lg T = lg(2π/k) + n lg r.
gradient = n and y-intercept = lg(2π/k)

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: Plot the six points of lg(T/10³ s) against lg(r/10⁸ m) (within half a small square), each with a vertical error bar.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: Draw a straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable line (steepest/shallowest line through all the error bars).

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer: gradient ≈ 1.5 (from Δy/Δx over more than half the line's length). Absolute uncertainty = gradient of best fit − gradient of worst acceptable line.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.answer: y-intercept ≈ 1.5 (substituting a point into y = mx + c). Uncertainty = difference between the two intercepts.

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer:
n = gradient = 1.5.
k = 2π/10^(y-intercept) ≈ 2 × 10⁸ (≈ √(GM) for Saturn, in SI units).
Uncertainty in n = uncertainty in gradient; uncertainty in k from the worst-line intercept.
